guide_enrichment.narrative:
Our numbers see Missouri’s defense as the clearest potential separator. Mississippi State has struggled to create scoring opportunities efficiently, while Missouri grades well at preventing them. The opener offered some supporting evidence, with Missouri holding Arkansas-Pine Bluff to 198 yards and three third-down conversions, but we are not treating that result as proof against stronger competition.

The uncertainty is on both sides of the ball for Missouri. Austin Simmons completed 17 of 19 passes with four touchdowns in his debut, but the offense returned only five starters and replaced its quarterback, center, a tackle and three starting receivers. The defense also returned just two starters after losing 10, so our strong longer-run defensive rating still has to be tested with a substantially different group. For us, the market is already accounting for Missouri’s advantages closely enough, and the available price does not create sufficient value.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch: We are watching Mississippi State’s passing offense against Missouri’s rebuilt defense. Our ratings favor Missouri in this matchup, especially when it comes to keeping opponents from turning drives into scoring chances. The question is whether that carries over with so much personnel turnover. Missouri did add experienced SEC starters Robert Woodyard Jr. at linebacker and Chris Graves Jr. at cornerback, but we need more evidence before treating the opening performance as confirmation.

recent_game.fact: Missouri opened the 2026 season with a 54-14 win over Arkansas-Pine Bluff on September 3.
Missouri outgained Arkansas-Pine Bluff 562-198, recorded 33 first downs and converted 6-of-10 third downs and both fourth-down attempts.
Missouri led Arkansas-Pine Bluff 40-0 at halftime after holding a 376-6 yardage advantage through two quarters.
Missouri rushed for 205 yards and passed for 357 yards in the opener.

opponent_notes.fact: Missouri is scheduled to play at Mississippi State on September 26, 2026, in an SEC game with kickoff listed in the 5-7 p.m. CT window.

quarterback.fact: Ole Miss transfer Austin Simmons started Missouri's opener and completed 17-of-19 passes for 252 yards, four touchdowns and no interceptions.
Simmons' 89.5% completion rate and 270.4 passer rating were the highest by a quarterback in a Missouri debut.
Simmons is the seventh different starting quarterback of the Eli Drinkwitz era and the third transfer quarterback.
Sophomore Matt Zollers is listed as Simmons' backup and completed 8-of-12 passes for 87 yards while adding a five-yard rushing touchdown in the opener.
Missouri lost 2025 starting quarterback Beau Pribula and added transfers Austin Simmons and Nick Evers to a quarterback room that also returns Zollers, who made three starts as a true freshman.

offensive_personnel.fact: Missouri's current first-team offensive line is listed as LT Cayden Green, LG Tristan Wilson, C Dominick Giudice, RG Curtis Peagler and RT Luke Work.
Missouri returned five offensive starters from 2025 and lost six, including quarterback Beau Pribula, center Connor Tollison, tackle Keagan Trost and three starting wide receivers.
Wide receiver Cayden Lee transferred from Ole Miss after starting all 15 games there in 2025; he caught five passes for 89 yards, including a 47-yard touchdown, in his Missouri debut.
Sophomore receiver Donovan Olugbode recorded career highs of seven receptions, 107 yards and two touchdowns in the opener.
Senior running back Jamal Roberts is listed first on the depth chart and had 13 carries for 47 yards and a touchdown against Arkansas-Pine Bluff.
Left tackle Cayden Green allowed two sacks, two quarterback hits and three hurries across 750 snaps in 2025, according to PFF.

defensive_personnel.fact: Missouri returned two defensive starters from 2025 and lost 10, including safety Jalen Catalon, defensive tackle Chris McClellan, linebacker Josiah Trotter, cornerback Toriano Pride Jr., edge Damon Wilson II and defensive end Zion Young.
Missouri added experienced SEC starters Robert Woodyard Jr. at linebacker and Chris Graves Jr. at cornerback; both started the 2026 opener.
Woodyard started 11 games for Auburn in 2025 and recorded 67 tackles, including 50 in conference play.
Graves appeared in all 41 Ole Miss games over the previous three seasons and made nine starts in 2025.
Linebacker Nicholas Rodriguez and safety Santana Banner finished second and third on Missouri in tackles in 2025 and are listed as 2026 starters.
Defensive tackles Marquis Gracial and Sterling Webb combined for 6.0 tackles for loss in 2025; Webb also had 2.5 sacks and six quarterback hurries.
Darris Smith recorded 4.0 sacks as a pass-rush specialist in 2025 and is listed as Missouri's starting JACK in 2026.

coaching_changes.fact: Chip Lindsey joined Missouri as offensive coordinator in December 2025 and is in his first season in the role.
Garrett Riley joined Missouri in January 2026 as quarterbacks coach after serving as Clemson's offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach.
John Papuchis became Missouri's special-teams coordinator and defensive assistant in January 2026 after six seasons coordinating special teams at Florida State.
Alex Atkins joined Missouri as tight ends coach in January 2026, and Chop Harbin joined as defensive line coach.
Derek Nicholson added co-defensive coordinator duties before the 2026 season while continuing to coach linebackers.

offensive_context.fact: Missouri averaged 228.3 rushing yards per game in 2025, ranking eighth nationally and first in the SEC.
Missouri produced a program-record 12 individual 100-yard rushing performances in 2025.
Missouri scored 31 rushing touchdowns in 2025 and opened 2026 with three rushing touchdowns against Arkansas-Pine Bluff.
In the 2026 opener, Missouri averaged 7.2 yards per play, converted 60% of its third downs and scored on all five red-zone possessions.

defensive_context.fact: Missouri's 2025 defense allowed 277.3 yards and 18.9 points per game, including 103.8 rushing yards and 173.5 passing yards per game.
Missouri limited Arkansas-Pine Bluff to 198 total yards, 89 rushing yards, 109 passing yards and a 3-of-13 third-down conversion rate.
Missouri forced five three-and-outs against Arkansas-Pine Bluff.
Missouri did not record a takeaway in its 2026 opener and committed one turnover.

special_teams.fact: Blake Craig is Missouri's returning placekicker and made a 32-yard field goal plus all seven extra-point attempts in the opener.
Brunno Reus is listed as Missouri's first-team punter, kickoff specialist and holder after the Tigers lost 2025 punter Connor Weselman.
DaMarion Fowlkes is listed as Missouri's primary punt and kickoff returner and had a 23-yard punt return in the opener.

series_context.fact: Missouri defeated Mississippi State 49-27 in Columbia on November 15, 2025.
Ahmad Hardy rushed 25 times for 300 yards and three touchdowns against Mississippi State in 2025.
Darris Smith recorded 3.0 tackles for loss against Mississippi State in 2025.

other_relevant.fact: Missouri entered the week 1-0 and ranked No. 25 in both the AP and Coaches polls.
Missouri was 30-10 since the start of the 2023 season after its 2026 opener.
Missouri had won 14 consecutive regular-season night games entering Week 2 of 2026.
